This section lists new types of armor found in the Northlands that are available to PCs, and it covers special rules regarding their use. The Armor table lists the cost, AC bonus, weight, and proficiency required for each kind of armor.

Beinagrind . This armor is formed by carving disks or short shingles out of whale or giant bones and lacing them to a backing of flexible leather.

Double Mail. Also called tvifold brynja, the rings of this chain mail are doubled, so each pair is passed through by four pairs of other rings. It is very heavy and bulky.

Hardened Mail Shirt. This chain shirt has rings of adamantine or mithral woven into key areas to provide more protection than normal mail.

Walrus Hide. These thick, treated walrus hide suits are flexible but quite heavy. In addition to its defensive benefits, walrus hide counts as winter clothing when determining the effects of extreme cold.

equipment.adventuringGearNotes:
This section covers standard nonmagical equipment and the rules for using it.

Jotunskull Helm . Favored by those who wish to project a fearsome aspect, these helms are fashioned from the cleaned bones of a sufficiently large giant. When you wear one, you have Advantage on Charisma ( Intimidation ) checks against Giants (at the GM’s discretion).

Skis . While wearing skis, you ignore Difficult Terrain from deep snow and move at double your normal Speed while going downhill in snow. You have Disadvantage on Dexterity saves and checks while wearing skis, except those related to moving through snow.

Skates . While wearing skates, you ignore Difficult Terrain from slippery ice and automatically pass Dexterity ( Acrobatics ) checks to avoid have the Prone condition on ice. You move at double your normal Speed while on ice, but you have a Speed of 5 feet off the ice.

Snow Goggles . These thick glasses are set with lenses of smoky glass, preventing snow blindness.

Snow Visor . These thick bone or wood visors are bound to the head and are constructed with a narrow slit for the wearer’s eyes. Creatures wearing snow visors have Immunity to snow blindness but have Disadvantage on Wisdom ( Perception ) checks relating to sight.

Snowshoes . While wearing snowshoes, you can ignore Difficult Terrain from deep snow. You have Disadvantage on Dexterity saves and checks while wearing snowshoes.

Talharpa . A musical instrument with two to four strings similar to a lyre and played with a bow.

equipment.mountsNotes:
Travel across the Northlands can be its own adventure. From howling blizzards to roaring giants, just moving from settlement to settlement pits the adventurer against nature and monsters alike. This section details various mounts and land vehicles the intrepid Northlanders use to travel.

###H3### Mounts

A mount can help you move more quickly through the wilderness, but it can also carry gear that would otherwise slow you down. The Mounts table shows each animal’s carrying capacity. See Chapter 8 for new mount stat blocks.

Mounts and Cargo . An animal pulling a carriage, cart, chariot, sled, or wagon can move weight up to five times its base carrying capacity, including the weight of the vehicle. If multiple animals pull the same vehicle, add their carrying capacities together.

Barding . Barding is armor designed for a mount. Any type of armor can be purchased as barding. The cost is four times the normal cost, and it weighs twice as much.

###H3### Land Vehicles

Land vehicles can travel on solid surfaces and across physical terrain. Much like the longships presented later, the land vehicles in this section have the following statistics.

Speed . The speeds in the table include movement during a combat round, miles per hour, and miles per day.

Crew . A vehicle typically has one driver, but other crew positions may be available. The minimum number of skilled hirelings needed to operate a vehicle depends on the type of vehicle, as shown in the table.

Passengers . The table lists the number of Small and Medium passengers the vehicle can accommodate.

Vehicle Repair . If a vehicle has taken damage and has fewer than half its hit points (rounded down), a creature can spend 1 hour or more and the necessary gp worth of spare parts to repair the damage. At the end of each hour, the vehicle regains Hit Points equal to its AC (up to the vehicle’s Hit Point Maximum). One hour of repairs requires spare parts worth a gp amount equal to 10 percent of the vehicle’s base cost, as shown on the Vehicle table.

###H4### Dog Sled

Dog sleds are long, narrow frames set on metal ski-like runners and pulled by teams of trained dogs. Ideal for crossing frozen terrain, dog sleds are commonly used in arctic regions for travel, trade, and transport.

A dog sled is a Large vehicle, weighs 150 pounds, has room on the back for one driver, and can hold 3 passengers or about 800 pounds of cargo. Sleds can be swift, but much depends on the terrain, snow conditions, and other obstacles.

Dog sleds typically have teams of dogs numbering between 6 and 10. For ease of play, use the stats for a wolf for an average sled dog. After 6 hours of travel, a sled dog must take a Long Rest or suffer one level of Exhaustion.

equipment.longshipsNotes:
The signature sea vessel of the Northlands is the iconic longship. Swift and agile in the water, longships are preferred by raiders, reavers, and Northern merchants of all sorts. Longships feature a removeable figurehead mounted on the prow, often carved to resemble a fearsome dragon or other beast, such as a raven or wolf, though some are sculpted as maidens, merfolk, and other aquatic creatures. The stern of the ship sports a carving as well, typically the tail of some fantastic monster.

All longships share a common design, with a keel, a stem at the prow and stern, and a hull. While many other ships have hulls with planks that meet edge-to-edge, a longship’s design overlaps the planks of the hull. This pattern, known as lapstrake or clinker-built, makes longships durable against rough waters. Longship keel designs vary, with some being flatter and able to traverse shallow water and others deeper for carrying more cargo. Longship designs also share rowing benches and oars, as well as a mast for a square sail. Oars allow the crew to quickly move a longship in and out of position, even bringing shallow-keeled ships onto shore. A steering rudder on the starboard side of a longship allows it to be directed easily, whether the ship is moving forward or backward.

Ship Action. At the end of each round, a vehicle with the required number of crew members can move up to its Speed and use one action. The section on Naval Combat in Chapter 7 details rules for fighting ship-to-ship as well as various shipboard actions. The specialized actions listed in the ship stat blocks in this section can be used as shipboard actions.

The longships presented in this section differ from the one found in the core rules.

###H3### Drakkar

The largest of longships, a drakkar is also called a “dragon ship” for its stylized dragon figureheads. Drakkar are the flagships of their fleet, and they are commissioned by jarls, chieftains, and other prominent, wealthy leaders.

The larger cargo hold of a drakkar also makes it ideal for long journeys. It is capable of carrying enough supplies to reach destinations that smaller longships would be ill-equipped for. However, drakkar are not as agile as other longships in terms of turning speed or in lighter wind conditions.

###H3### Karvi

The smallest of the flat-keel longships, the karvi can traverse shallow waters to transport goods, fish, and even raiders. While a karvi can be used in battle, it is often used as a general-purpose river and coastal ship. Its size and shallow keel make it less ocean-worthy than other longboats. While a knarr is used for transporting livestock, it is common to find a karvi ferrying people to their destination.

magicItems.name: Antlered Headband of Chernobog
magicItems.rarityNote: Requires Attunement by a Bard, Paladin, Sorcerer, or Warlock
magicItems.summary: Wondrous Item, Legendary (Requires Attunement by a Bard, Paladin, Sorcerer, or Warlock)
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Legendary (Requires Attunement by a Bard, Paladin, Sorcerer, or Warlock)

Bone-white antlers, the tips stained with dried blood, are mounted on a tanned leather headband stained with the black ichor that oozes from the bases of the antlers.

While wearing this headband, you gain the following benefits.

Devil’s Sight. You can see normally in Dim Light and Darkness —both magical and nonmagical—within 120 feet of yourself.

Antler Charge. You can make a melee weapon attack with the antlers. Add your Proficiency Bonus and your Strength modifier to the attack roll. The antlers deal 1d10 Piercing damage plus your Strength modifier. The antlers have the Push Weapon Mastery property, and you get it for free (with the antlers only) if you do not have access to Weapon Mastery as a class feature. If you have Weapon Mastery as a class feature, you can use Push with the antlers. If you do, you push creatures hit by your attacks with the antlers 15 feet instead of 10 feet.

If you move at least 15 feet in a straight line before dealing damage to a creature with the antlers, that creature must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the Frightened target repeats the save, ending the effect on a success.

Spells. The headband has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can take a Magic action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it using your spell save DC: Darkness (1 charge), Dominate Monster (3 charges). You can target Undead creatures with this use of Dominate Monster , even if they ordinarily have Immunity to it.

magicItems.name: Arm Ring of Self-Sacrifice
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare (Requires Attunement)

This arm ring is mildly painful to wear. This arm ring has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While you are wearing it, you can use its charges as follows:

Aggressive Strike. When you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend 2 charges to deal maximum damage with the attack. However, you also take Force damage equal to the minimum possible damage of the attack, and you cannot reduce or mitigate this damage in any way.

Redirection. When a creature you can see makes an attack roll against an ally within 5 feet of you, you can use your Reaction and expend 1 charge to become the target of the attack instead.

magicItems.name: Arrow of Ice-Trapping
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Arrow), Rare

This arrow deals an additional 1d6 Cold damage on a successful hit. If a creature takes damage from the ammunition, it must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Restrained condition due to being trapped in bands of ice. It can make a save at the end of each of its turns to end the Restrained condition. While it has the Restrained condition, the target takes 1d6 Cold damage at the start of each of its turns. The target or a creature within reach of it can take an action to make a DC 15 Strength ( Athletics ) check to free it.

magicItems.name: Ashbraid
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Battleaxe, Greataxe), Very Rare (Requires Attunement)

This axe has a fire-blackened blade, and its haft is wrapped with strands of unbreakable golden hair. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon. The weapon deals an extra 1d6 Fire damage on a hit.

When you hit a creature with an attack made with this magic weapon, the target has Vulnerability to Fire damage until the beginning of your next turn. If the target has Resistance to Fire damage, it loses that until the beginning of your next turn, though it does not have Vulnerability to Fire damage. This has no effect on creatures with Immunity to Fire damage.

magicItems.name: Bell-Ringing Greatclub
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Greatclub), Uncommon

This Greatclub is fashioned from the clapper of a giant’s bell. When you score a Critical Hit with this Greatclub, you can choose for the target to have the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn instead of dealing the extra damage from the Critical Hit.

magicItems.name: Belt of the Berserker
magicItems.rarityNote: Requires Attunement by a Barbarian with the Reckless Attack Class Feature
magicItems.summary: Wondrous Item, Rare (Requires Attunement by a Barbarian with the Reckless Attack Class Feature)
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare (Requires Attunement by a Barbarian with the Reckless Attack Class Feature)

While wearing this wolf-hide belt, you can choose to use the following feature each time you activate your Rage class feature:

Foolhardy Rage. While you are Raging, you gain an extra Bonus Action each turn that you can only use to extend your Rage or to take the Dash action. If you use it to take the Dash action, you cannot take the Dash action again on that turn. In addition, you gain a +1 Bonus to your Rage Damage. Finally, you must use your Reckless Attack Class feature on each of your turns during your Rage, or your Rage ends.

magicItems.name: Berserker’s Mead
magicItems.body:
Potion, Rare

For 1 minute after you consume this potion, you are Immune to the first 40 points of damage you take.

magicItems.name: Blade of Insults
magicItems.summary: Weapon (Any Simple bladed weapon), Rare (Requires Attunement by a Bard)
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Any Simple bladed weapon), Rare (Requires Attunement by a Bard)

A bard wielding this weapon is empowered to mix swordplay with witty repartee. If you deal damage with this weapon on your turn, you can use your Bonus Action to cast Vicious Mockery at the same creature you damaged. If you wish, as part of that Bonus Action, you can also expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration, which otherwise functions as it normally would.

magicItems.name: Bygul’s Paw Boots
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

These fluffy boots have wide soles and sharp spikes along the front that act as crampons. While wearing the boots, you can move through Difficult Terrain caused by snow or ice without expending additional movement, automatically pass Dexterity ( Acrobatics ) checks to avoid having the Prone condition, and you have Advantage on Strength ( Athletics ) checks to climb. While wearing the boots your footprints resemble those of a large cat.

magicItems.name: Cloak of Wide-Ranging
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Common

While wearing this wolf-skin cloak, you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws to avoid levels of Exhaustion after traveling for more than 8 hours in a day.

###H4### Magic Items (D-G)

magicItems.name: Defender Honey
magicItems.body:
Potion, Uncommon

The honey is light brown and has a smooth sweetness. For 10 minutes after you consume this honey, you can use your Reaction to put yourself between an attack that would hit an ally within 5 feet of you. The attack targets you instead with the same attack roll.

magicItems.name: Einherjar’s Drinking Horn
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

This ornately carved drinking horn has 6 charges and regains 1d6 charges each day at dawn. It appears empty, but the holder can expend a charge to take a Magic action and put it to their lips to drink a draught of delicious mead. Any creature drinking this mead is invigorated, gaining enough nourishment to sustain it for a day. Alternatively, a creature can drink from the horn as a Magic action and expend 6 charges to gain the same benefits, and the horn removes 1 level of Exhaustion from that creature. A creature cannot benefit from this reduction in Exhaustion more than two days in a row.

magicItems.name: Feather Token
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rarity varies

The following are additional feather token options:

Raven (Uncommon). You can use a Magic action to throw this black token into the air. You can see and hear through the token for one hour. The token disappears afterwards or if the distance between you and it exceeds 1 mile. The bird has the statistics of a raven .

Snowy Owl (Uncommon). You can use a Magic action to wave this white and grey feather across a creature’s face. For 1 hour, that creature can take the Hide action without the usual requirements of being Obscured or behind Cover, as long as it is against snowy terrain.

magicItems.name: Glacierpress Boots
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Very Rare

The furry uppers of these boots have ice and gravel matted into them that never melts. These boots have 3 charges and regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the boots, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge to activate them for 1 hour. While the boots are active, you can move in a straight line through the space of any creature smaller than Huge. You do not provoke Opportunity Attacks due to this movement. The first time you enter a creature’s space during this move, it must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be pushed ahead of you for the rest of your move.

magicItems.name: Goggles of Snowsight
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

While wearing these multifaceted blue crystal goggles, you do not have Disadvantage on Wisdom ( Perception ) checks to see through areas that are Lightly Obscured by blowing snow, sand, or other debris.

magicItems.name: Goggles of Tracking
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

These goggles have multiple lenses that can be swiveled. The goggles have 3 charges. While wearing the goggles, you can take a Magic action to expend a charge. For 1 hour, you can see any tracks that were obscured by natural phenomena such as rain, snow, or blowing sand in the last week. In addition, you have Advantage on ability checks to track creatures. The goggles regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

magicItems.name: The Grave Blade
magicItems.summary: Weapon (Longsword), Fabled (5th-level and higher properties require attunement)
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Longsword), Fabled (5th-level and higher properties require attunement)

The reavers of Wolfheim brought home many strange treasures as souvenirs and mementos from their campaigns abroad. A dwarven warrior named Essalla claimed a strange sword as her share of the spoils on one such raiding journey. Unusual in design and unadorned by dwarvish standards, it seemed destined to be a souvenir brought out only when tales of the campaign were to be told.

This sword has a dull, lifeless grey blade, and the hilt is carved from aged bone. The guard is made from ribs, and the pommel is sourced from the rounded end of a femur, both cast in bronze

The Grave Blade became known in different tales, for the threads of fate of each bearer seemed to be cut short soon after taking possession of it. It has changed hands many times over the next nine years, seemingly taken from a corpse as often as it was exchanged for gold or favors.

The blade is known for the song it hums in the presence of undead, and with the death of its carriers, the blade’s song grows ever more insistent. Some say the song is a warning, while others theorize that it wants to be found and interred with the body of its first bearer.

The souvenir of so much death was lost among a merchant’s wares that never reached their destination in Wolfheim, and the mystery of its song persists in tales told on dark nights when the fire burns low.

The pommel of this sword hums a wordless song that can be heard within a 5-foot radius when Undead are within 60 feet of it. As your level increases, it has the following additional properties if you are wielding it or holding it while attuned to it:

5th level. When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 Hit Point instead. If the damage came from a creature, you have Advantage on attack rolls against it for 1 minute. Once used, the sword can’t be used in this way again until the next dawn.

9th level. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this sword. In addition, the sword deals an additional 1d6 Necrotic damage on a hit.

13th level. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls (instead of +1) with this sword. In addition, when the sword deals damage to a living creature, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

17th level. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls (instead of +2) with this sword. If you make a successful attack roll against a creature that has 50 Hit Points or fewer, you can compel it to die. Once used, the sword can’t be used in this way again until the next dawn.

Fabled Magic Items

Fabled magic items are distinct as a rarity. A fabled item grows in power alongside the character who wields it. Rules for fabled items are summarized here, and a few fabled magic items can be found in this chapter.

A fabled magic item begins as a Common magic item. The item grants a minor, useful trait to its owner that doesn’t require attunement to use.

To access any higher-level trait, a PC must attune to it using standard Attunement rules. Once attuned, a PC can use the fabled item’s more powerful properties as they increase in level. If a PC higher than 1st level attunes to a fabled item, its level-dependent properties, up to the character’s current level, are immediately available.

At the GM’s discretion, an item’s more powerful properties might become available only after the character completes a particular quest or event related to the item’s story rather than immediately upon reaching each property’s required level.

If a PC chooses not to attune to a fabled item, it remains a common magic item, granting only its minor property, regardless of the character’s level.

Unless otherwise noted, properties granted by a fabled item are in effect as long at the character is wearing, carrying, or touching the item.

###H4### Magic Items (H)

magicItems.name: Hel’s Coin
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Common

While carrying this blackened silver coin, if you fail a Death Saving Throw, you treat the save as a success instead. Then the coin crumbles into dust.

If you carry more than one Hel’s Coin, you gain the following curse instead. If you succeed on a Death Saving Throw, you treat the success as a failure. Then one Hel’s Coin crumbles to dust. This curse remains until there is only one coin left in your possession, whereupon that coin’s normal effect resumes. You can freely divest yourself of extra coins.

magicItems.name: Hjartarydi’s Belt
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

Touching this blood-red leather belt fills you with a sense of comfort. While you have the belt equipped, you have Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

magicItems.name: Hollow Eye
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare (Requires Attunement)

This small wooden talisman is shaped like a large eyeball with an empty void in place of the pupil. While holding the eye, as a Magic action, you can expend 1 of your Hit Dice to drip a small quantity of your own blood into the eye and cast either the Arcane Eye spell or the Divination spell. Once you use the eye once, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Honey of the Hearth Fire
magicItems.body:
Potion [Honey], Uncommon

When you consume this honey, you end the Blinded , Deafened , Frightened , and Poisoned conditions on yourself.

magicItems.name: Honey of the Hive Warden
magicItems.body:
Potion [Honey], Very Rare

When you consume this honey, you have Resistance to Poison for 1 hour. Once during the duration, you may cast Insect Plague (DC 15). Instead of locusts dealing Piercing damage, the spell creates bees that deal Poison damage.

magicItems.name: Honey of the Norn-Blessed
magicItems.body:
Potion [Honey], Rare

When you consume this honey, you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws for 1 hour. Once during the duration, you may cast Augury .

magicItems.name: Honey of Robust Health
magicItems.body:
Potion [Honey], Common

When you consume this honey as part of a Short Rest, you can reroll any result of 1 or 2 on Hit Dice spent to regain Hit Points during that rest. You must use the new roll. The honey has a deep red tinge and a rich flavor, and it warms the stomach.

magicItems.name: Honey of the Sacred Bear
magicItems.body:
Potion [Honey], Rare

When you consume this honey, you have Advantage on Strength checks for 1 hour. Once during the duration, you may cast Heroism on yourself, requiring no Concentration .

magicItems.name: Honey of the Skald’s Tongue
magicItems.body:
Potion [Honey], Rare

When you consume this honey, you have Advantage on Performance and Persuasion checks for 1 hour. Once during the duration, you may cast Suggestion (DC 15).

magicItems.name: Horn of Battle’s Call
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare

This leather-wrapped horn is bound with stout iron bands. When you blow this horn as an action, choose up to five allies within 120 feet of you who can hear you. Each target has Advantage on melee weapon attacks until the start of your next turn and gains 10 Temporary Hit Points . The Frightened condition ends on all targets. Once you blow the horn, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Horn of the Hrimthursar
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare

This ivory horn, also known as the Horn of Frozen Breath, is typically carved from the bone of a white dragon, remorhaz, or another arctic monster. When you sound the horn, it creates a blast of freezing wind in a 60-foot Cone . Each creature in the Cone takes 4d6 Cold damage and has the Incapacitated condition until the start of your next turn. A successful DC 15 Constitution saving throw halves the damage and negates the Incapacitated condition. Once you blow the horn, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Horn of the Wild Hunt
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Legendary

This black horn appears normal during daylight, but in darkness it glitters like a starlit sky. The horn has 4 charges and regains 1d4 charges daily at sunset.

When you blow this horn, you can expend 1 charge to cast Conjure Animals , or 3 charges to cast Conjure Fey (conjuring a spectral hunter).

###H4### Magic Items (I)

magicItems.name: Icebreaker Axe
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Battleaxe or Greataxe), Rare

This axe is forged from a dark grey metal and has blue-white runes inscribed on the head. This weapon deals an extra 3d8 Thunder damage to any object made of ice that it hits.

The weapon has 3 charges. As a Magic action, you can strike the weapon against an icy surface to create a 60-foot Line of thunderous energy. Each creature in the Line must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or have the Prone condition. Objects in the Line that are made of ice take 3d8 Thunder damage. The weapon regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

magicItems.name: Iced Steel Armor
magicItems.summary: Armor (Any Medium or Heavy armor made primarily of metal), Uncommon
magicItems.body:
Armor (Any Medium or Heavy armor made primarily of metal), Uncommon

This suit of armor is made of iced steel, which legends hold originates in the frozen underworld of Niflheim. Objects made of iced steel always feel cold to the touch. While you are wearing it, you automatically succeed on saving throws against Extreme Heat , and you have Advantage on saving throws against spells involving fire and heat.

magicItems.name: Iced Steel Weapon
magicItems.summary: Weapon (Any Ammunition or Melee Weapon), Common
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Any Ammunition or Melee Weapon), Common

This weapon or piece of ammunition is made of iced steel, which legends hold originates in the frozen underworld of Niflheim. Objects made of iced steel always feel cold to the touch. Damage you deal with this weapon is treated as Cold damage rather than the type the weapon normally deals, if it would be advantageous to you.

magicItems.name: Incendiary Coal
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare

This lump of coal is pleasingly warm to the touch. As a Magic action, you breathe gently into the coal to ignite it and can then throw it up to 30 feet, where it blossoms into a 5-foot Sphere of fire.

A creature that ends its turn within or adjacent to the Sphere must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 1d6 Fire damage on a failure and half as much on a success. Flammable objects in or adjacent to the Sphere that aren’t being worn or carried start burning.

At the end of each of your subsequent turns, the size of the Emanation increases by 5 feet, and the Fire damage dealt increases by 1d6 until it reaches its maximum size of 30 feet and maximum damage of 6d6. At the end of each of your turns after that, the size of the Emanation decreases by 5 feet, and the Fire damage dealt decreases by 1d6 until both reach 0, at which point the coal cannot be used again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Iron Traitor’s Arm Ring
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Very Rare

This arm ring has the rough appearance of hammered iron. You can take a Utilize action to swing the arm ring at a Huge or smaller creature within 5 feet of yourself.

Make a melee attack roll with an attack bonus equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus. On a hit, the arm ring coils around the target’s arm, and the magical properties of magic items held or worn by the target cease to function until you take a Bonus Action to issue a command that releases the arm ring.

A creature that can touch the arm ring, including the one wearing it, can take an action to make a DC 20 Strength ( Athletics ) check to remove the arm ring. On a successful check, the item is removed, and the creature is freed from its effect. On a failed check, any further attempts made by that creature automatically fail until 24 hours have elapsed. The arm ring can also be removed if the limb is severed or if the ring is destroyed.

Once the arm ring is used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

###H4### Magic Items (K-P)

magicItems.name: Kempdomr Axe
magicItems.summary: Weapon (Battleaxe, Bearded Axe, Breidox, or Greataxe) Rare (Requires Attunement)
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Battleaxe, Bearded Axe, Breidox, or Greataxe) Rare (Requires Attunement)

This axe channels the might of the jotun. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

This weapon has 5 charges. When you hit an enemy with a melee attack using this weapon, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra 3d8 Force damage and push the target 10 feet away from you for every size category it is smaller than Gargantuan (Gargantuan creatures are not pushed). The weapon regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn.

Giant’s Boon. While you are attuned to the weapon and wearing either a Belt of Giant Strength or Gauntlets of Ogre Power to which you are also attuned, the weapon regains all expended charges daily at dawn. In addition, the bonus to attack and damage rolls increases to +2, and the extra Force damage you deal when you expend a charge increases to 4d8.

magicItems.name: Laekning Shield
magicItems.body:
Round Shield, Uncommon

While holding this Shield , you have a +1 bonus to Armor Class, in addition to the Shield’s normal bonus to Armor Class. This round Shield magically repairs itself and is not destroyed at the end of an encounter where you are struck.

magicItems.name: Mug of Friendship
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Common

You can use a Magic action to enchant any potable liquid within this flagon. A creature that drinks the enchanted liquid is Friendly to you, and you have Advantage on Charisma ( Persuasion ) checks against it for 1 hour. After the hour is over, the creature is still Friendly, though it’s attitude can change based on your behavior.

After it has been used to enchant liquid once, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Nine-Escape Knot
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare

This one-foot-long rope of woven fox tails channels the power of the trickster Loki to escape difficult situations. While you hold it or have it on you, you have Advantage on checks or saving throws made to avoid or end the Grappled or Restrained conditions.

Unraveling. As a Magic action, you can unravel one of the nine knots in the rope to cast one of the following spells, using Charisma as your spellcasting ability: Calm Emotions , Charm Person , Confusion , Disguise Self , Enthrall , Feign Death , Greater Invisibility , Mirror Image , and Misty Step . Each of these spells may be cast only once by the item. When the last knot is unraveled, the rope loses its magic.

magicItems.name: Northlander’s Boots
magicItems.summary: Wondrous Item, Common (Requires Attunement) The wearer of these furred boots can use a Bonus Action to transform them into snowshoes, ice skates, or skis, and back again.
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Common (Requires Attunement)
The wearer of these furred boots can use a Bonus Action to transform them into snowshoes, ice skates, or skis, and back again.

magicItems.name: Ottaveggr Talharpa
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Common

This Northlands Lyre is strung with cords made of braided jotun hair. As a Magic action, you can play the talharpa to grant all your allies within 60 feet who can hear it Advantage on saves against the Frightened condition and on Strength ( Athletics ) checks for 1 hour. Once this ability has been used, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Potion of Near-Death Portent
magicItems.body:
Potion, Very Rare

This potion’s cloudy grey fluid has a golden thread suspended in it. Drinking this potion gives you a vague vision of your potential death. The next time within 1 hour that you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can use a Reaction and roll 1d20. If the roll is 10 or higher, you take no damage. If the roll is less than 10, you are reduced to 1 hit point instead.

magicItems.name: Prismatic Ammunition
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Any Ammunition), Uncommon

This piece of ammunition is made of prismatic steel infused with the power of the Bifrost. When you hit a creature that is outside of its home plane with a ranged attack with this ammunition, it is banished to its home plane for 1 round.

magicItems.name: Prismatic Steel Armor
magicItems.summary: Armor (Any Medium or Heavy armor made primarily of metal), Uncommon, (Requires Attunement)
magicItems.body:
Armor (Any Medium or Heavy armor made primarily of metal), Uncommon, (Requires Attunement)

This suit of armor is made of prismatic steel infused with the power of the Bifrost. While you are wearing it, you automatically succeed on saving throws against effects that would push, pull, teleport, or otherwise move you against your will.

While attuned to the armor, you can take a Magic action to teleport the armor onto or off of your body, even if it is on another plane of existence from you. When you teleport the armor off of your body, it moves to an adjacent square. You can’t use this effect again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Prismatic Steel Weapon
magicItems.summary: Weapon (Any Melee Weapon), Very Rare (Requires Attunement)
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Any Melee Weapon), Very Rare (Requires Attunement)

This weapon is made of prismatic steel infused with the power of the Bifrost. When you hit a creature that is outside of its home plane with a melee attack using this weapon, they are banished to their home plane for 1 round. If you score a Critical Hit with this weapon against a creature that is outside its home plane, the creature is banished to its home plane indefinitely, though it can leave of its own accord.

While attuned to the weapon, you can take a Bonus Action to summon it to your empty hand, even if it is on another plane of existence.

###H4### Magic Items (R)

magicItems.name: Rage Hammer
magicItems.summary: Weapon (Maul or Warhammer), Uncommon (Requires Attunement by a Barbarian)
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Maul or Warhammer), Uncommon (Requires Attunement by a Barbarian)

When you enter a Rage, you can make a melee attack with this weapon as part of the Bonus Action used to enter the Rage. After using this property, you can’t use it again until you complete a Short Rest.

magicItems.name: Ravenflight Axe
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Handaxe), Uncommon (Requires Attunement)

When you attack a creature with this Handaxe and one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the weapon deals an extra 1d6 Slashing damage.

Swarm Attack. Once per day, you can release the weapon from your hand as an action, at which point it transforms into 60-foot Cone of swarming ravens. Make a ranged weapon attack with the axe against each creature of your choice in the Cone. Immediately after completing the last attack, the weapon reappears in your hand. This property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Reaver’s Lodestone
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

This stone has a hole drilled through its center, through which runs a leather thong. One end of the stone has the rune for “person” etched into, and the other bears the rune for “gold.” The stone has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. As a Magic action, you can spend 1 charge and whisper “person” or “gold” and dangle the stone from the thong.

When using the command “person,” the stone orients and gently pulls toward some number of people. The strength of the pull is stronger when the targets are closer or higher in quantity. The range is 1 mile per gathering of 100 humanoid people, 10 miles for 1000 people, or 100 miles for 10,000 people. A gathering is a temporary or permanent living community, such as a hamlet, village, or town.

When using the command “gold,” the stone orients and pulls you toward valuables. The strength of the pull is stronger when the targets are closer or more valuable. The range is 10 feet for coins or art objects worth a total of 100 GP, 100 feet for coins or art objects worth a total of 1000 GP, or 1000 feet for coins or art objects worth a total of 10,000 GP.

Whether you use it to find people or gold, it pulls you for 1 minute.

magicItems.name: Ring of the Cragtop Jarl (Jarlpact)
magicItems.body:
Ring, Very Rare (Requires Attunement)

This polished granite ring bears runes of strength. While wearing the ring, when you attack with a weapon that deals Bludgeoning damage, you score a Critical Hit on a natural 19 or 20.

In addition, the ring has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend its charges to use the properties below.

Bones of the Mountain. You can expend 1 charge to cast False Life .

Mountain Strike. You can expend 1 charge when you deal Bludgeoning damage with a melee or ranged attack to push the target 10 feet.

Finally, it has the following property.

Jarlpact Benefit. If an ally within 120 feet is attuned to and wearing any other Ring of the Jarlpact, you have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

magicItems.name: Ring of the Diving Bird
magicItems.body:
Ring, Uncommon

While wearing this ring, you have a Swim Speed equal to any Fly Speed you have.

magicItems.name: Ring of the Forgefire Jarl (Jarlpact)
magicItems.body:
Ring, Very Rare (Requires Attunement)

This black iron ring bears glowing orange runes of fire and metal. While wearing the ring, your melee weapon attacks deal 1d6 extra Fire damage on a hit.

In addition, the ring has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend its charges to use the properties below.

Furnace Blast. You can expend 1 charge to cast Burning Hands (level 4 version).

Echo of the Forge. You can expend 1 charge to cast Heat Metal (level 4 version).

Finally, it has the following property.

Jarlpact Benefit. If an ally within 120 feet is attuned to and wearing any other Ring of the Jarlpact, you have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

magicItems.name: Ring of the Glacial Jarl (Jarlpact)
magicItems.body:
Ring, Very Rare (Requires Attunement)

This glittering ring of blue-white crystal bears runes of ice and battle. While wearing the ring, your melee weapon attacks deal 1d6 extra Cold Damage on a hit.

In addition, the ring has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend its charges to use the properties below.

Frozen Wrath. You can expend 1 charge to cast Ice Storm . You are immune to any damage dealt by this casting of the spell, and you ignore the Difficult Terrain created by it.

War Cry. You can expend 1 charge after you hit with a melee weapon attack to grant Advantage on all attacks made by allies who can see or hear you against the creature you hit. This effect lasts until the start of your next turn.

Finally, it has the following property.

Jarlpact Benefit. If an ally within 120 feet is attuned to and wearing any other Ring of the Jarlpact, you have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

Jarlpact Rings

Long ago, a set of rings was crafted to help cement a truce between warring tribes of giants. Four rival giant jarls met to don their rings in a show of peace. However, the truce lasted only until the celebratory feast, when the drunken jarls started a brawl that became a bloody combat. The rings shattered along with the peace, but fragments of the original artifacts shaped themselves into smaller versions of the rings and scattered across the Northlands.

In addition to their base powers, each ring grants an additional jarlpact benefit if at least one other jarlpact ring is attuned to a nearby ally. This benefit doesn’t apply to multiple rings worn by the same character.

magicItems.name: Ring of Hospitality
magicItems.body:
Ring, Common

This ring is fashioned to show two hands shaking in greeting. While wearing this ring, you have Advantage on Charisma ( Persuasion ) checks when you take the Influence action to request shelter from another creature that can understand you.

magicItems.name: Ring of Ice-Shielding
magicItems.body:
Ring, Rare (Requires Attunement)

This ring has 3 charges, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can use a Reaction to form a 5-foot square, 1-foot-thick wall of ice when you are the target of an attack or are required to make a Dexterity saving throw. The wall provides Three-Quarters Cover . If the attack misses or you succeed on your save, the ice wall explodes. Any enemies adjacent to it take 1d6 Piercing damage and 1d6 Cold damage.

magicItems.name: Ring of Surtr
magicItems.body:
Ring, Uncommon

This ring is roughly forged from a single wrapped shard of coal-black iron. It is warm to the touch. When you deal Fire damage to an object while wearing this ring, you deal an extra 1d8 Fire damage.

magicItems.name: Ring of the Tempest Jarl (Jarlpact)
magicItems.body:
Ring, Legendary (Requires Attunement)

This ring is made from a twisted piece of wood charred by lightning, and it bears runes of the storm and the sea. While wearing it, you have Resistance to Cold, Lightning, and Thunder damage.

In addition, the ring has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend its charges to use the properties below.

Storm Strike. You can expend 2 charges when you deal damage with a melee attack. In addition to the weapon’s normal damage, the target takes 8d6 Lightning damage, and it has the Blinded condition until the start of your next turn.

Windborne Leap. You can expend 1 charge to cast the Jump spell on yourself.

Finally, it has the following property.

Jarlpact Benefit. If an ally within 120 feet is attuned to and wearing any other Ring of the Jarlpact, you gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

magicItems.name: Rod of Frostbite
magicItems.summary: Wand, Rare (Requires Attunement by a Spellcaster)
magicItems.body:
Wand, Rare (Requires Attunement by a Spellcaster)

This rod is made of blackened, desiccated skin shrunk tightly around a humanoid forearm and hand. This wand has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn.

Withering Cold. While holding it, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge to cause a shadowy ray to streak from one of the rod’s fingertips toward a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or for 1 minute, it takes an additional 2d6 Necrotic damage whenever it takes Cold damage. At the end of each of the target’s turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Cast Spell. You can cast Ray of Frost from it using your spell attack modifier. The damage scales with your level.

magicItems.name: Rostungr Armor
magicItems.body:
Armor (light or hide), Very Rare

You have a +1 bonus to Armor Class while wearing this armor. You can take a Bonus Action to cause the armor to envelop you for 1 minute. You grow flippers and a thick layer of blubber, which remain for the duration. While in this state, your Speed is halved, you have Swim Speed of 30, and you have Resistance to Bludgeoning damage. Once this action is used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Rumbling Hammer
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Maul or Warhammer), Common (Requires Attunement)

Immediately after you score a Critical Hit with this hammer, it casts Thunderclap , using your level to set the cantrip’s damage. Your allies have Immunity to the damage dealt by this casting of the spell.

###H4### Magic Items (S)

magicItems.name: Salt of Thawing
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Common

You can use a Magic action to spread this salt on 5-foot square area within 10 feet of you. Ice up to 1-foot thick in that area instantly melts.

magicItems.name: Sail of Favorable Winds
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

These gorgeous sails are embroidered with swirls and contours to make them appear like fluffy white clouds. While sailing, a ship flying these sails treats any wind as though it were a tailwind, coming from straight behind the ship, and thus can maintain maximum speed without the need to tack or adjust the sails. This has no effect if the ship is becalmed and there is no wind available at all.

magicItems.name: Sealskin Armor
magicItems.body:
Armor (Any Light), Uncommon (Requires Attunement)

You have a Swim Speed equal to your normal Speed when wearing this armor. Also, you have Advantage on any checks and saves to avoid or end the Grappled condition.

magicItems.name: Seidr Rune Necklace
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare (Requires Attunement)

This necklace is made of carved runes strung with giant’s hair. The runes glow faintly blue. While wearing this necklace, you can take a Magic action to learn and influence the future of one individual that you are familiar with.

You choose a type of situation from battle, diplomacy, trade, trickery, or other situation. The GM tells you if that individual is likely to encounter such a situation today. For the remainder of the day, you know when that individual is in that type of situation, and as Reaction, you may add or subtract 1d10 from a die roll they just made during that event, though you have no additional knowledge of what transpired where the individual is.

You may not take this Magic action again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Serpent Fin Oars
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

These silvery enchanted oars are lighter and stronger than typical wooden oars and come in sets sufficient to outfit a single ship. While sailors are rowing these oars, the ship’s pilot has Advantage on checks to control the ship.

When a ship outfitted with these oars is adjacent to another rowed ship, the ship can take an Action to slash that ship’s oars, destroying them.

As long as at least one of the oars is unbroken, and that oar remains on the ship, 1 additional oar is magically produced each dawn until there are enough to outfit the ship.

magicItems.name: Shadow Blade
magicItems.summary: Weapon (Longsword, Rapier, Scimitar, or Shortsword), Rare (Requires Attunement)
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Longsword, Rapier, Scimitar, or Shortsword), Rare (Requires Attunement)

This sleek magic weapon projects a shadowy double image of itself when wielded. The weapon has 3 charges and regains 1d3 charges each day at sunset.

Elusive Strike. When you miss with a melee attack made with this weapon, you can spend 1 charge to reroll the attack roll and use the new result.

Phantasmal Parry. While holding this weapon, you can spend 1 charge to cast the Shield spell.

magicItems.name: Shield of the World Serpent
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Very Rare (Requires Attunement)

This shield is shaped from a scale of Jormungandr. While wielding the shield, you cannot be pushed or pulled against your will. At the start of each of your turns, you may end any Grappled and Restrained conditions on you.

magicItems.name: Skinchanger Arm Ring
magicItems.summary: Wondrous Item, Fabled (5th-level and higher properties require attunement)
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Fabled (5th-level and higher properties require attunement)

This arm ring is made from copper and is covered with a patina that cannot be removed.

There was once a sect of Northern warriors dedicated to learning from the animals in their region. Each member of the order sought to exemplify the capabilities and spirit of their chosen animal. The raven warrior was keen to observe and could travel far and fast. The follower of the wolf fought well in conjunction with others. Others had strength and endurance like bears.

These ideals were forged into an enchanted arm ring worn by the leader of the sect. Whether this magic was achieved with the aid of dwarves, druids, or sorcerers, none can say. With experience, the wearer of the arm ring could shapeshift into one of the three animals exemplified by the warriors.

Though the order won many victories on the battlefield, they couldn’t be held in the employ of any one jarl. The wilds called to them, and they visited the settled lands of the North less and less as the years went by, until they were never seen again.

While wearing this arm ring, you can comprehend and verbally communicate with ravens, wolves, and bears of all varieties so long as they are Beasts, and you can use any of the Influence action’s skill options with them.

As your level increases, you gain the following benefits while wearing this arm ring.

5th level. You can take the Magic action to grow black-feathered wings and gain a Fly Speed of 50 feet for 1 hour. While you have these wings, your size decreases by one category—from Medium to Small, for example. You also have Disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Your attacks with weapons or Unarmed Strikes deal 1d4 less damage on a hit (this can’t reduce damage below 1). You can end the effect early as a Bonus Action. Once used, the arm ring can’t be used in this way again until the next dawn.

9th level. You have Advantage on attack rolls with melee weapons and Unarmed Strikes against a creature if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn’t have the Incapacitated condition.

13th level. You can use a Magic action to give yourself Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your level. You also gain Resistance to Cold damage until the Temporary Hit Points are depleted or you finish a Long Rest. Once used, the arm ring can’t be used in this way again until the next dawn.

17th level. The arm ring has 3 charges. You can take a Magic action and spend 1 charge to cast the Polymorph spell on yourself. The forms you can take are limited to a raven ; wolf or dire wolf ; or black , brown , or polar bear . When you cast Polymorph in this way, you retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. The arm ring regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

magicItems.name: Slip-Bane Bracelet
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Common

This corded bracelet has 1d4 + 2 tiny claws hanging from it. While wearing it, you can use your Reaction to halve damage from falling. Doing so causes one of the claws to crumble. Once all of the claws are gone, the bracelet crumbles to dust.

magicItems.name: Songsteel Armor
magicItems.body:
Armor (Any), Uncommon

Metal armor made of songsteel rings like a bell or chime when it clangs against an object. When wearing the armor, you can call out to Volund as a Bonus Action. Until the end of your next turn, you take 5 less damage from all attacks that hit you. Once you use this feature, you must finish a Long Rest before you can use it again.

magicItems.name: Songsteel Shield
magicItems.body:
Armor (Shield), Uncommon

Metal shields made of songsteel rings like a bell or chime when they clang against an object. When holding the shield, you can call out to Volund as a Bonus Action. Until the end of your next turn, you have a +5 bonus to your AC. Once you use this feature, you must finish a Long Rest before you can use it again.

magicItems.name: Songsteel Weapon
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Any), Uncommon

A metal weapon made of songsteel rings like a bell or chime when it clangs against an object. When wielding the weapon, you can call out to Volund as a Bonus Action. Until the end of your next turn, you gain a +5 bonus to damage rolls with this weapon. Once you use this feature, you must finish a Long Rest before you can use it again.

magicItems.name: Snowbirds
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Uncommon

These three crystal figures of terns can interlock into a circle as if nestling together. Each one can be removed and buried in snow or a similarly loose material like sand or soil. As a Magic action, you can call to a buried crystal bird within 100 feet of you. It bursts up into the air, filling a 10-foot-tall, 5-foot-radius Cylinder with snow, before falling back to the ground. The area within the snow burst is Heavily Obscured until the start of your next turn. The three snowbirds can be placed separately and activated simultaneously to obscure multiple areas.

magicItems.name: Storrbani
magicItems.summary: Weapon, Fabled (5th-level and higher properties require attunement)
magicItems.body:
Weapon, Fabled (5th-level and higher properties require attunement)

Thogar Giant-Hewer earned great renown through unwavering bravery but not intellectual brilliance. His unmatched courage often forged far ahead of his reason. As a youth, he could not prevent marauding giants and trolls from destroying his village and murdering his family. Left alone on the blood-soaked snow, a fire kindled deep in Thogar’s heart. From that day, he unwaveringly sought vengeance against giantfolk, not for glory or renown but in the hope his daring might earn him friends or even a new family of his own.

The Giant-Hewer became a terror to trolls and giants alike. Though not the strongest warrior and certainly never the wisest, he braved troll dens and giant camps, throwing himself into battle where others paused to strategize. Yet time and again, the people he saved turned cold. His deeds, though brave, were rarely welcome. His plans resulted in the death of everyone but himself. His traps lured giants to their doom at the expense of entire villages. Those he rescued offered no feasts of thanks, only wary glances and closed doors. The more he gave, the more alone he became, yet still he fought on believing if he was only brave enough, he could win through to find a new family.

Thogar met his end in his own typical fashion. After running across the trail of a band of storm giants heading toward a village, he foolishly attacked them in the settlement square. His blade, Storrbani , slew many giants before the others fled, but unfortunately, the fires ignited by the battle burned down half the village. Thogar’s shattered body lay in the remains of the wedding feast (to which the giants had been invited), and no one came to his aid or to witness his last breath. Skalds say he died utterly alone, but when the Valkyries came to collect him, he did not wish to enter Valhalla alone. Taking pity on the brave warrior, they cast his spirit into his blade, binding it there until the day he falls again, fighting beside a true friend, so together they might enter the Hall of Golden Shields side by side.

This longsword is supernaturally light and easy to use. Its weight is reduced to 1 pound, and it gains the Finesse weapon property. Sparks trail from Storrbani ’s blade as though it were a burning branch. When you hit a target with Storrbani, the target takes an extra 1d4 Fire damage as the blade burns upon impact.

As your level increases, you gain the following benefits while wielding or holding this weapon.

5th level. The rune Gebo appears on the blade. As a Bonus Action, you can touch the rune and cast Shield of Faith on a creature (besides yourself) you can see within 60 feet. You don’t need to Concentrate on the spell to maintain it. Once used in this way, you must finish a Short Rest before you can use it again.

In addition, the spirit of Thogar Giant-Hewer awakens within the longsword. It becomes a sentient, Lawful Neutral weapon with Intelligence 8, Wisdom 13, and Charisma 10. It has hearing and vision out to a range of 60 feet. It communicates telepathically with its wielder, and it can speak in a gravelly voice much like an angry growl. It can read and understand Common and Giant. Thogar’s spirit is passionate but not particularly bright. It wants the wielder to confront giants and trolls, and (secretly) to fall in glorious battle against the forces of Jotunheim so that wielder and blade may feast and fight together in eternal Valhalla. It urges its wielder to seek out and destroy evil trolls and giants, and to never back down from a fight. If its wielder displays cowardice or refuses an opportunity to battle an evil troll or other giant, the spirit sulks, suppressing the magical properties of the weapon until the following dawn.

9th level. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon, and the amount of Fire damage it deals increases to 2d6. In addition, the rune Tiwaz appears on the blade. As a Bonus Action, you can touch this rune and give the extra Fire damage from this blade to the weapon of a creature you can see within 60 feet. At the end of your next turn, the Fire damage property returns to Storrbani .

13th level. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon instead of a +1 bonus. In addition, the rune Thurisaz appears on the blade. As a Bonus Action, you can touch this rune. When you do so, your attack rolls with this magic weapon score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 until the end of your next turn. If the target is a creature of the giant type, Storrbani deals an extra 1d8 damage on a critical hit.

17th level. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon, instead of a +2 bonus. In addition, the rune Ansuz appears on the blade. As a Bonus Action, you can touch the rune and gain Immunity to all damage until the end of your next turn. Once used, the sword can’t be used again in this way until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Stormbinder’s Cloak
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Legendary (Requires Attunement)

You have Resistance to Cold, Lightning, and Thunder damage while wearing this cloak. You also ignore any Obscurement created by magical or non-magical clouds, fog, or mist. Lastly, whenever you cast a level 1 + spell that deals Cold, Lightning, or Thunder damage, you may treat the spell as if you had cast it with a spell slot 1 higher than the slot used.

magicItems.name: Stormhook
magicItems.summary: Weapon (Dart, Javelin, or Spear), Rare (Requires Attunement)
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Dart, Javelin, or Spear), Rare (Requires Attunement)

When you hit a creature with a ranged attack made with this magic weapon, the target is pulled 10 feet closer to you. If the target has a Fly Speed, that Speed is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.

After making a ranged attack with this weapon, it returns to your hand.

magicItems.name: Stormhorn
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare

This wooden horn is carved from lightning-struck yew. It has 6 charges and regains 1d6 charges each day at dawn. It can be blown as a Magic action to cast a spell— Fog Cloud (1 charge), Gust of Wind (2 charges), Sleet Storm (3 charges)— using your spell save DC.

magicItems.name: Sustaining Belt
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Common

This wide belt has short, soft grey fur on both its inner and outer faces, with a long strap bearing many more punch holes than an ordinary belt. While wearing this belt, you don’t have to consume as much food or water. You can go an additional number of days equal to your Constitution modifier before you suffer the effects of starvation or dehydration.

###H4### Magic Items (T)

magicItems.name: Tireless Armor
magicItems.body:
Armor (Any), Rare (Requires Attunement)

This armor has 3 charges and regains 1d3 charges daily at dawn. Each time you would receive a level of Exhaustion , you may spend a charge to negate that Exhaustion.

As long as the armor has at least 1 charge remaining, you cannot take penalties to your Speed.

magicItems.name: Tireless Rower
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Very Rare

Appearing to be merely a copper statue of a seated dwarf, this duergar marvel is actually a magic and clockwork automaton. When the command word is spoken, the device duplicates itself until there are enough dwarves to row the entire ship. A single tireless rower can replace the rowing crew of a longship for 8 hours. It needs to recharge for 8 hours before it can be used again.

magicItems.name: Titancall Dagger
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Dagger), Legendary (Requires Attunement)

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a creature with this Dagger , you can summon a frost giant as a Bonus Action. When you do, specify a target for the giant’s ire.

The giant appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 120 feet of yourself and is convinced that the target has wronged them. While summoned, the giant is Friendly to you and your allies.

The giant remains for 1 hour or until it drops to 0 Hit Points, at which time it vanishes. After a giant is summoned, the dagger can’t be used again in this way until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Tordalfr’s Rebuttal
magicItems.summary: Javelin, Fabled (5th-level and higher properties require attunement)
magicItems.body:
Javelin, Fabled (5th-level and higher properties require attunement)

Tordalfr was a storm giantkin born to a human mother in a small village. After years of jibes and taunts from the children of local warriors, he snapped.

Brael, son of the village headman, and a pompous, aspiring warrior, called Tordalfr out in public, proclaiming to his assembled cronies that there was irrefutable evidence that Tordalfr was the unwanted child of forbidden lovers, and defying anyone present to offer proof to the contrary.

Tordalfr’s fury reached such a pitch that the cloudless sky opened up and a bolt of lightning struck his outstretched hand, coalescing into the form of a throwing spear, which he hurled at his tormentor. The javelin struck Brael in the chest, hurling him backward and leaving a blackened, smoking crater where his heart had been. Tordalfr marched furiously from the village and never returned.

When you hit with a ranged weapon attack using this Snaerispear , you may push the target up to 10 feet directly away from you.

As your level increases, you gain the following benefits while wielding or holding this weapon.

5th level. Immediately after hitting or missing an enemy, this javelin reappears to your hand.

9th level. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon. In addition, when thrown, the javelin is wreathed in electricity, dealing an extra 1d6 points of Lightning damage to any target it hits.

13th level. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon instead of +1. In addition, you can use a Bonus Action to charge your next attack with the weapon with electricity. The next time you hit with this javelin before the end of your turn, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or have the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you complete a Short Rest.

17th level. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon, instead of +2. In addition, when you hit with this weapon, you can call down a bolt of lightning from the heavens to strike the target. This bolt deals 8d8 Lightning damage to the target and all creatures within 15 feet of it. Creatures within the blast radius are pushed 15 feet away from the target. Once used, this ability can’t be used again until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Trollkin Unguent
magicItems.body:
Potion, Rare

One vial of this oil can cover one Medium or smaller creature, along with the equipment it’s wearing and carrying (one additional vial is required for each size category above Medium). Applying the oil takes 10 minutes. The affected creature then has Resistance to Fire damage for 1 hour.

If the creature takes Fire damage, it becomes wreathed in ghostly green flames that shed Dim Light in a 15-foot radius. While ablaze, the creature’s melee weapon attacks deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage. After 10 minutes, the flames die out and the oil’s effects expire.

This oil is transparent with a rainbow sheen.

magicItems.name: Tyr’s Crushing Might
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Rare

This iron bowsprit is forged in the shape of the one-handed god Tyr in the moments after he lost his hand to the Fenris wolf. His wounded arm is hugged tight to his body, his sword thrust forward in the other, and a mighty cry upon his lips. While equipped with this item, a ship can take the Ram action for double the normal damage, and it takes no damage to itself from Ramming.

###H4### Magic Items (V-W)

magicItems.name: Valhallan Armor
magicItems.summary: Armor (Any Medium or Heavy), Rare (Requires Attunement)
magicItems.body:
Armor (Any Medium or Heavy), Rare (Requires Attunement)

While wearing this armor, you don’t have the Unconscious condition when you are at 0 Hit Points. You still make Death Saving Throws normally. You can’t use the Help action to make a Medicine check to stabilize yourself.

magicItems.name: Warrior Honey
magicItems.body:
Potion [Honey], Common

When you consume this honey, you have Advantage on the first Initiative check you make during the next hour. You also have Advantage on the first melee attack roll you make. The honey has small bubbles throughout and tingles in your stomach.

magicItems.name: Warhammer of Giant Felling
magicItems.body:
Weapon (Warhammer), Very Rare

This Warhammer is inscribed with runes and pictograms dedicated to battles between dwarves and giants. You have a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

If you hit a creature that is a larger size than you with this weapon, that creature must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or take 3d6 Thunder damage and have the Prone condition.

If you hit a creature that is your size or smaller, that creature must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or take 2d6 Thunder damage and have both the Prone and Restrained conditions as it is driven into the ground. The target or a creature within reach of it can take an action to make a DC 15 Strength ( Athletics ) check to free it.

magicItems.name: Winged Helm of Wisdom
magicItems.body:
Wondrous Item, Very Rare (Requires Attunement)

Two black bird wings sweep back from the sides of this unusual silver helm, which has an unbroken smooth plate where the right eye hole would be, though the magical properties of the helm allow you to see through it. While wearing the helm, you can take a Magic action to gain a Fly Speed of 60 ft. for 1 hour. If you are flying when the duration expires, you descend at a rate of 30 feet per round until you land. While this effect is active, you may maintain Concentration on two spells at once, and the plate where the right eye hole would be glows a ghostly blue. This ability cannot be used again until the next dawn.

spells.name: Aegir’s Breath
spells.summary: You blow a cloud of frigid air at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Cold damage, or 1d12 if the target is at least partially submerged in water.
spells.body:
Evocation Cantrip (Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard)

Casting time: Action

Range: 120 feet

Components: V, S

Duration: Instantaneous

You blow a cloud of frigid air at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Cold damage, or 1d12 if the target is at least partially submerged in water.

Cantrip Upgrade. The spell creates two clouds at level 5, three clouds at level 11, and four clouds at level 17. You can direct the clouds at the same target or at different ones. Make a separate attack roll for each cloud.

spells.name: Angrboda’s Fury
spells.summary: When you cast this spell, you open yourself up to become a conduit of the rage of the giant goddess Angrboda. One creature within range makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target becomes Vulnerable to one type of damage of your choice. If the creature has Immunity
spells.body:
Level 4 Transmutation (Cleric, Sorcerer, Wizard)

Casting time: Action

Range: 30 feet

Components: V, S

Duration: Concentration , up to 1 minute.

When you cast this spell, you open yourself up to become a conduit of the rage of the giant goddess Angrboda. One creature within range makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target becomes Vulnerable to one type of damage of your choice. If the creature has Immunity to the damage type you selected, it loses its Immunity and takes damage as normal, but it does not have Vulnerability to the damage type you chose.

The creature can repeat the Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending this spell on a success.

spells.name: Aspect of the Narwhal
spells.summary: A willing creature that you touch takes on the aspects of a narwhal. It grows flippers and a long horn-like tusk. The target gains Resistance to Cold damage while submerged in water, its Speed becomes 5 feet, and it gains a Swim Speed of 50 feet. The target can take a Bonus Actio
spells.body:
Level 2 Transmutation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)

Casting time: Action

Range: Touch

Components: V, S

Duration: Concentration , up to 10 minutes

A willing creature that you touch takes on the aspects of a narwhal. It grows flippers and a long horn-like tusk. The target gains Resistance to Cold damage while submerged in water, its Speed becomes 5 feet, and it gains a Swim Speed of 50 feet. The target can take a Bonus Action on any turn in which it moves at least 15 feet directly toward an enemy to make a gore attack that deals Piercing damage equal to 2d6 plus its Strength modifier.

spells.name: Awaken Ship Guardian
spells.summary: You summon a protective spirit to live within the hull of a Large or larger ship. While the spell lasts, the ship has the following benefits:
spells.body:
Level 8 Conjuration (Cleric, Druid)

Casting time: Action

Range: 30 feet

Components: V, S

Duration: 24 hours

You summon a protective spirit to live within the hull of a Large or larger ship. While the spell lasts, the ship has the following benefits:

Immunity to Fire damage.

Each time the ship takes damage from a Large or larger creature, the attacking creature makes a Wisdom saving throw, taking 5d6 Psychic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

As a Bonus Action while you are on the ship, you can expend a spell slot, and the ship regains Hit Points equal to three times the slot level plus your spellcasting modifier.

spells.name: Bearstormer
spells.components: V, S, M (a pinch of bear fur)
spells.summary: You create three phantasmal grizzly bears in a 20-foot Cube within range. Until the spell ends, you can use a Bonus Action to move the Cube up to 40 feet.
spells.body:
Level 5 Illusion (Bard, Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)

Casting time: Action

Range: 120 feet

Components: V, S, M (a pinch of bear fur)

Duration: Concentration , up to 1 minute

You create three phantasmal grizzly bears in a 20-foot Cube within range. Until the spell ends, you can use a Bonus Action to move the Cube up to 40 feet.

When the Cube appears, each enemy in it makes an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 18 (4d8) Psychic damage and has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only. A creature also makes this save when the spell’s area moves into its space and when a creature enters the spell’s area or ends its turn there. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You increase the size of the Cube by 20-feet, the number of phantasmal bears by two, and the damage by 9 (2d8) for each spell slot level above 5th.

spells.name: Beast of Ragnarok
spells.components: V, S, M (a bezoar formed in a wolf’s stomach)
spells.summary: The spectral aura of Fenris surrounds you as you draw Ragnarok to the world for a moment. Until the spell ends, the sky grows dark, casting the world in Dim Light in a 1-mile Sphere centered on you. Thick snows fall inside the Sphere, causing the ground to become Difficult Terrai
spells.body:
Level 9 Conjuration (Cleric, Druid, Warlock, Wizard)

Casting time: Action

Range: Self

Components: V, S, M (a bezoar formed in a wolf’s stomach)

Duration: 1 minute

The spectral aura of Fenris surrounds you as you draw Ragnarok to the world for a moment. Until the spell ends, the sky grows dark, casting the world in Dim Light in a 1-mile Sphere centered on you. Thick snows fall inside the Sphere, causing the ground to become Difficult Terrain and vision to be Heavily Obscured .

You gain the following benefits for the Duration:

You see clearly within the Sphere and are unaffected by the Difficult Terrain caused by the spell.

You have Advantage on all d20 Tests .

All creatures have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

You have Immunity to all types of damage except for one. Roll a d12 to randomly determine a damage type (1. Acid, 2. Bludgeoning, 3. Fire, 4. Force, 5. Lightning, 6. Necrotic, 7. Piercing, 8. Poison, 9. Psychic, 10. Radiant, 11. Slashing, or 12. Thunder.) You have Vulnerability to the damage type you roll.

You have Advantage on saving throws to resist or end all conditions.

spells.name: Bergelmir’s Provocation
spells.castingTime: Reaction, which you take when you see a creature make an attack or spell attack
spells.summary: The creature making the attack must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature makes the attack against a different eligible target of your choice, which cannot include the creature itself. If there is no other eligible target, the creature’s attack is wasted.
spells.body:
Level 3 Enchantment (Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard)

Casting time: Reaction, which you take when you see a creature make an attack or spell attack

Range: 60 feet

Components: V

Duration: Instantaneous

The creature making the attack must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature makes the attack against a different eligible target of your choice, which cannot include the creature itself. If there is no other eligible target, the creature’s attack is wasted.

spells.name: Beseech the Norns
spells.components: V, S, M (a silver spindle worth 100+ GP, which the spell consumes)
spells.summary: You contact one of the three Norns, the weavers of fate, to intercede on your behalf by altering the past, present, or future. Choose one of the following effects:
spells.body:
Level 4 Divination (Cleric)

Casting time: Bonus Action

Range: Self

Components: V, S, M (a silver spindle worth 100+ GP, which the spell consumes)

Duration: Special (see text)

You contact one of the three Norns, the weavers of fate, to intercede on your behalf by altering the past, present, or future. Choose one of the following effects:

Change the Past (Uror). Choose a creature you can see that died since the start of your last turn. That creature is returned to life with 1 Hit Point. This spell can’t revive any creature that has died of old age, nor does it restore any missing body parts.

Guide the Present (Verthandi). Treat the first attack roll or ability check you roll before the end of your turn as a natural 20.

Shape the Future (Skuld). Beginning at the start of your next turn and lasting for 1 minute, you have Advantage on all ability checks and saving throws.

If you cast the spell more than once before finishing a Long Rest, there is a cumulative 25 percent chance for each casting after the first that the spell has no effect (other than to consume the material component).

spells.name: Billowing Sails
spells.summary: You touch a ship or other wind-powered vehicle and fill its sails with a strong breeze. Whenever the ship travels by sail, its Speed increases by 10 ft. or by 1 mph.
spells.body:
Level 2 Evocation (Druid, Ranger, Sorcerer, Wizard)

Casting time: 1 minute or Ritual

Range: Touch

Components: V, S

Duration: Concentration , up to 8 hours

You touch a ship or other wind-powered vehicle and fill its sails with a strong breeze. Whenever the ship travels by sail, its Speed increases by 10 ft. or by 1 mph.

spells.name: Bone-Chilling Smite
spells.castingTime: Bonus Action, which you take immediately after hitting a creature with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike .
spells.summary: The target takes an extra 3d8 Necrotic damage from the attack, and it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or gain one level of Exhaustion until the spell ends.
spells.body:
Level 3 Necromancy (Paladin)

Casting time: Bonus Action, which you take immediately after hitting a creature with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike .

Range: Self

Components: V

Duration: 1 minute

The target takes an extra 3d8 Necrotic damage from the attack, and it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or gain one level of Exhaustion until the spell ends.

At the end of each of its turns, the Exhausted target repeats the save. On a success, it removes all Exhaustion caused by this spell. On a failure, it receives one level of Exhaustion.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 3rd.

spells.name: Bound Fortunes
spells.components: V, S, M (two small spindles bound together with thread)
spells.summary: You touch another willing creature and bind your fates together until the spell ends. For the duration, if the target is within 60 feet of you and makes an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you may use your Reaction to allow the target to reroll and use the new result.
spells.body:
Level 5 Necromancy (Cleric)

Casting time: Action

Range: Touch

Components: V, S, M (two small spindles bound together with thread)

Duration: Concentration , up to 1 hour

You touch another willing creature and bind your fates together until the spell ends. For the duration, if the target is within 60 feet of you and makes an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you may use your Reaction to allow the target to reroll and use the new result. The target can do the same to you. Each time you do this, your, and only your Hit Point maximum is reduced by 1d4, and the same is true of the target. If this reduces your Hit Point maximum to 0, you die. This reduction is removed when the spell ends.

spells.name: Bragi’s Theatrical Fall
